requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:12-48 covers the contract: no-op on null/'' (`! is_string($webhookUrl) || $webhookUrl === ''`), `Http::timeout(5)->post($webhookUrl, ['content' => $text])`, `key=value` lines joined with "\n", `mb_substr(..., 0, 1800)`, error log on non-2xx with status only, catch Throwable plus `scrub()` of the URL. Redaction (lines 128-149) matches the case-insensitive key list including api_key/api-key/apikey, the Bearer regex `/Bearer\s+\S+/i`, and recursive nested arrays rendered as JSON. config/logging.php:203 sets the stack default to 'daily'; lines 211-217 add the audit channel (daily driver, logs/audit.log, level env LOG_AUDIT_LEVEL default info, days env LOG_AUDIT_DAYS default 90); there is no discord channel. config/services.php:230-232 adds the discord webhook_url; .env.example and phpunit.xml:305 pin LOG_STACK=daily. The `daily` channel itself (14 days via LOG_DAILY_DAYS) is not in the diff, so I could not verify it. It is probably the stock Laravel config.

conventions.evidence: Docs are kept in sync: docs/ops/logging.md is new with a decision guide, CHANGELOG.md:29 has an entry under [Unreleased], and .env.example has the new keys. The class sits where the contract puts it (app/Ops). The public `send()` has no PHPDoc, although the conventions ask for PHPDoc on touched public methods. No domain writes, Livewire code or migrations are involved.

security.evidence: The webhook URL never goes into logs: the non-2xx path logs only `'status' => $response->status()` (DiscordOpsAlert.php:38-40), and the exception path logs the class name and a scrubbed message (lines 43-46). Sensitive keys and Bearer strings are redacted at the top level and in nested arrays, and Stringable objects are checked too (lines 85-88). `scrub()` only does an exact `str_replace` of the URL, so a URL-encoded or partial URL in an exception message would get through. The risk is limited.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php covers resolvability, the no-op for null and '', the POST URL and exact content, truncation to exactly 1800, redaction (password, api_key, Bearer, nested token, readable queue) and the non-2xx error log without the URL. Gaps: the transport-exception path and its URL scrubbing are untested (no `Http::fake` that throws ConnectionException). The audit test is vacuous (`expect(true)->toBeTrue()`, lines 404-408). Nothing asserts the logging config contract: no discord channel, stack containing daily, audit days/level/path.

simplicity.evidence: One small class using the built-in HTTP client and Log facade, with no extra abstractions. `formatValue` (lines 84-128) is somewhat long, with separate branches for bool/null/object/fallback json_encode, and its scalar redaction logic overlaps with `redactArray`. Acceptable.

readability.evidence: Small, clearly named private helpers (`isSensitiveKey`, `containsBearerCredential`, `scrub`, `redactArray`), no dead code or debugging output. `formatValue` is the longest method but still easy to follow.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: .env.example, CHANGELOG.md, app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php, config/logging.php, config/services.php, docs/ops/logging.md, phpunit.xml and the test. The notifier is not wired into any job or handler, as the task requires.

issues.explanation: Nothing tests the transport-exception path, where the exception message is scrubbed of the webhook URL. That is the security-relevant branch most likely to leak the token.
The audit-channel test only asserts `expect(true)->toBeTrue()`. It checks neither the channel's config (driver daily, path audit.log, days 90, level info) nor that the write reaches the file.
No test covers the logging config contract: stack channels containing 'daily', no `logging.channels.discord`, and the daily channel keeping 14 days.
The diff does not touch the `daily` channel, so I could not verify the requirement of 14 days via LOG_DAILY_DAYS. It probably comes from the stock Laravel config.
`scrub()` only replaces the exact URL string, so a URL-encoded or truncated form in an exception message would not be redacted.
The new public `send()` method has no PHPDoc, although the conventions ask for PHPDoc on public methods.

review.summary: The change adds App\Ops\DiscordOpsAlert, which no-ops when unconfigured, formats `key=value` lines, truncates multibyte-safely to 1800 characters, redacts sensitive keys, Bearer strings and nested arrays, and soft-fails with URL-free error logs. It also adds the audit log channel, switches the stack to daily, and updates the env and docs. The implementation looks correct and stays within scope. The tests miss the exception/scrub path, the audit test is vacuous, and nothing checks the logging config contract, so I would approve it with requested follow-ups.
